faq.a: Baasim is associated with the Arabic form بَاسِم, whose core sense is baasim; smiling.

faq.q: What is the origin of Baasim?
faq.a: Baasim is associated with Arabic. Baasim is Arabic بَاسِم (Bāsim), the active participle of بَسَمَ, meaning 'smiling'.
Yes — the underlying form بَاسِم is Arabic.
Baasim can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Baasim should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Bāsim is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.a: In Urdu, Baasim is rendered باسم and carries the sense باسم، مسکراتا ہوا.

faq.q: What does Baasim mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Baasim is rendered باسم and carries the sense باسم، خندان.

faq.q: What are the variants of Baasim?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Baasim, baasim, basim. Script forms are باسم, بَاسِم, बासिम.

faq.q: Is Baasim a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
